title: Copilot Studio: interactive MCP apps render inside agent conversations
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, governance paths, commands and consumption-based licensing are supported. The changed MCP documentation still supports the distinction between automatic standard-harness tool updates and manually refreshing the Microsoft Copilot harness connection.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns rich interactive app experiences in Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Deliver rich interactive app experiences in Copilot Studio agents

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The preview target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The General Availability target is November CY2026, not a committed release date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents are planned to render interactive UI inline when calling a UI-enabled tool on a compatible MCP server.
claims.quote: When an agent calls a UI-enabled tool from a compatible MCP server, interactive experiences like sortable tables and drilldowns render directly in the conversation.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives sortable tables and drilldowns as examples of experiences inside the conversation.
claims.quote: interactive experiences like sortable tables and drilldowns render directly in the conversation

claims.quote: A plain-text fallback keeps the agent working on surfaces that can't render the UI

claims.claim: MCP is a standard for exposing tools to an agent.
claims.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard for exposing tools to an agent.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: An MCP server can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Blocking an MCP server disables all its tools across the organization under that management route.
claims.quote: Select **Block** to restrict the server across your organization, or **Unblock** to restore access to a previously blocked server.

claims.claim: The beta package block API is subject to change and unsupported in production.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the package block API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a [Microsoft Agent 365](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365) license.

claims.quote: Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.quote: Reject a pending Copilot package title submission. This action reviews a package title and its submitted version; it doesn't reject an individual user's request.

claims.quote: Replace `{packageId}` with the title ID confirmed for reviewing the pending submission. Don't substitute an individual request identifier.

claims.claim: Connector blocking follows Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Add an environment > Available > environment > Add to policy > Next > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block.
claims.quote:
Select the three dots (**⋮**) next to the connector, and then:

    - To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select **Block**.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Classification Blocked -Connectors <connector-objects> classifies connectors as blocked.
claims.quote: The name of the group to which the connectors should be added. Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Each connector object passed to Add-ConnectorsToPolicy must contain id, type and name.
claims.quote: The list of connectors to add to the policy. Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties:

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy moves connectors already classified in another group to the specified group.
claims.quote: If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: The data policy page does not mention MCP apps specifically.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCP apps" "Copilot Studio" "admin" "disable". Read admin-data-loss-prevention, including scope, MCP connector blocking and configuration steps; it names connected MCP servers but not MCP apps.

claims.claim: After choosing Block, the data policy creation flow continues through Next, scope if prompted, Next, review and Create policy.
claims.quote: Review your policy, and then select **Create policy** if you're creating a new policy or **Update policy** if you're editing an existing policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center governs supported agent tools, while Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls, so a block is not assumed to apply across products.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 provides administrative controls for supported tools. Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components. An approval or block doesn't necessarily apply across all products or connected components.
